clue.text: He kills two idiots in the end

indicators.note: the end tells us the little word in goes last, after the two fools

parts.note: an ass is a fool, and there are two of them
the second of the two fools, another ass
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grim tale of a killer who disposes of a pair of fools at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the end' looks like 'finally', but it tells you to put IN at the end, after ASS twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A murderer is someone who kills, usually for hire or politics.

clue.text: Inventor places metal discon the starting-place

parts.note: a paten is the metal plate or disc used for the bread at Communion
in golf the tee is where each hole is started

explanation.surface: An inventor sets a metal disc down where a golfer begins.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'places ... on' puts PATEN on top of TEE. The newspaper text runs 'disc on' together.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone granted a patent on a device is its registered inventor.

clue.text: Principle route for progress

parts.note: read as principal, the head of a school or college
a way is a road or route

explanation.surface: A guiding rule that shows the path to advancement.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay needs 'Principal' (head teacher), not 'Principle' as printed.
explanation.definitionFit: Making headway means moving forward, advancing against difficulty.

clue.text: A delivery vehicle at sea

parts.note: a float is a small delivery van, as in a British milk float

explanation.surface: A van used for deliveries finds itself out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: A milk float is the small electric van that once delivered milk to British doorsteps.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the water and not sunk is to be buoyant, sailing at sea.

clue.text: Ages with hesitation one might use this when mistaken

definitions.text: one might use this when mistaken

parts.note: eras are long periods of time, ages
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: After long pauses and umming, someone reaches for a tool to fix their error.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber is used to remove a pencil mistake from paper.

clue.text: Wordy encounter in heraldic corridor

parts.note: a passage is a corridor in a building
heraldry deals with coats of arms, so heraldic gives the phrase of arms

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out in a hallway hung with family crests.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage of arms is a fight, here a verbal dispute or argument.

clue.text: Non-operatic co, arranged this musical work

indicators.note: arranged as music is reworked, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A company sets out a musical piece that is not an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges NONOPERATICCO into the answer; 'arranged' also fits the musical surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece for soloist at the keyboard with orchestra is a classic concert work.

clue.text: Such a period of instruction would not be foreign for students in Madrid

definitions.text: Such a period of instruction would not be foreign for students in Madrid

parts.words: Such a period of instruction would not be foreign for students in Madrid
parts.note: a class in a foreign language, which for pupils in Spain's capital is their own tongue

explanation.surface: Madrid pupils find one class is in no way foreign to them.
explanation.definitionFit: A class teaching the language of Spain is native, not foreign, to Spanish pupils.

clue.text: Give up occupation

parts.note: occupation read as living in a place, so giving it up means moving out

explanation.surface: Someone resigns from their job.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave a house or room empty is to surrender its occupancy.

clue.text: Condemns for a time this old book

parts.note: dooms means condemns to a bad fate
a day is a period of time

explanation.surface: A medieval record that passes sentence on people for a set period.
explanation.walkthrough: The Domesday Book, the 1086 survey of England, is also spelt this way.
explanation.definitionFit: William the Conqueror's great survey of England is the famous old record book.

clue.text: Absence of tungsten at the present time

parts.note: absence of something means there is no such thing
W is the chemical symbol for tungsten

explanation.surface: A chemist notes that the metal is currently missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening currently is happening at this moment.

clue.text: Stays close to the body?

parts.note: stays are the stiffening strips in a tight undergarment, which sits snug on the torso

explanation.surface: Someone remains near a corpse.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiffened undergarment, once called stays, is laced tightly around the torso.

clue.text: A hormone perhaps for the space traveller

parts.note: many hormones, such as testosterone, are steroids

explanation.surface: An astronaut is given a hormone supplement.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor planet is a rocky body travelling through space.

clue.text: Some terribly human thing to do

indicators.note: some of the word terribly is taken, a run of letters from inside it

explanation.surface: A remark that behaving terribly is only human.
explanation.walkthrough: From the saying 'to err is human, to forgive divine'.
explanation.definitionFit: Making mistakes is proverbially human, as Pope wrote.

clue.text: Elasticated doorman?

parts.note: a doorman at a club who throws people out, and something springy that rebounds

explanation.surface: A nightclub doorman made of rubber.
explanation.definitionFit: A club's door guard ejects troublemakers; something stretchy springs back.

clue.text: Caught with William in a Welsh valley

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
Wm is the standard abbreviation for the name William

explanation.surface: A man named William is caught in a Welsh valley.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh for a hollow, a deep rounded basin among mountains, also called a cirque.

clue.text: Lazy or bashful after the performance

indicators.note: after places the word for bashful behind the word for performance

parts.note: a work is a performance or production
shy means bashful

explanation.surface: An actor is either idle or timid after the show.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who avoids labour is idle.

clue.text: Race hindrance

parts.note: a barrier that runners must get past, giving its name to a kind of race

explanation.surface: Something that slows down a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrier or impediment that runners in a race must clear.

clue.text: Monarch's joint aptitude for regal duties

parts.note: a king is a monarch, here with a possessive
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A ruler with a bad hip shows his talent for ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: The role and qualities of a ruler of a realm.

clue.text: Manner a round object was stuffed up a jumper

indicators.note: stuffed means filled, so the other pieces go inside the word for manner

parts.note: a way is a manner of doing something

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for round object is read bottom to top

parts.note: a ball is a round object

explanation.surface: Something round was crammed into a sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns BALL into LLAB; A plus LLAB goes inside WAY. 'jumper' is not a sweater but a hopping animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A small kangaroo is a hopping marsupial of Australia.

clue.text: Matches a variety of outlines

indicators.note: a variety is a different version, so these letters are given in another order

explanation.surface: A range of matches come in different shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of schema, a diagram or plan in outline.

clue.text: One or other that is up on the right

indicators.note: in a down clue up reads the abbreviation for that is bottom to top

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, meaning that is
taken as written

explanation.surface: A choice of two, written up on the right-hand side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns IE into EI, which sits on THE and R in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Either means one or the other of two.

clue.text: Bill, an officer on the road is in agreement

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
CO is a commanding officer
RD is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A bill and a policeman on the road reach agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in accord is to be in harmony or concord.

clue.text: Fiery entertainer?

parts.note: a performer of songs, and also something that scorches, like a flame

explanation.surface: A passionate performer with a hot temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A vocalist entertains; something that scorches would be one that singes.

clue.text: All one might bid for

definitions.meaning: an item at auction is put up as a numbered ...

explanation.surface: Everything you might put in an offer for at auction.
explanation.definitionFit: Used for 'everything' (the whole lot), and for an item offered at an auction.

clue.text: Finding fault with the judge, a newcomer

parts.note: a critic judges the merit of works
L is for learner, a novice, as on British L-plates

explanation.surface: A judge and a newcomer are both looking for faults.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for learner, from the L-plates British learner drivers show.
explanation.definitionFit: Being censorious means pointing out flaws.

clue.text: Endlessly help one town in Italy

indicators.note: endlessly means the final letter of the word for help is removed

parts.note: assist means help
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone helps one Italian town ceaselessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' looks like it modifies help but chops T from ASSIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Hill town in Umbria, home of St Francis.

clue.text: Anti-establishment free-for-all

parts.note: an unconcealed uprising against authority, a revolt in plain view

explanation.surface: A chaotic brawl against those in power.
explanation.definitionFit: An unconcealed uprising against authority is a revolt carried out in the open.
